//namedInputs: production: what a package's build reads of it, and so what a package that inlines or runs it rebuilds on (`^production` in the plugins' build inputs): its sources and manifests, never its docs, specs or plugin note. Without it, an edit to a library's CONTEXT.md rebuilt every plugin that inlines the library (#93).
//release: One version for every plugin, cut together and tagged v<semver> (ADR-0005, #90). The version lives in the tag, never in a commit: main keeps every version at 0.0.0. `nx release version` writes the next version into the working tree, from the conventional commits since the last tag, and touches git no further. site:release-publish packs and publishes that tree. `nx release changelog` then tags HEAD, pushes the tag and writes the GitHub release, which is the changelog; there is no changelog file. With no commit, the push sends only the tag, so releases run in CI, where HEAD is main as the remote has it (.github/workflows/release.yaml). Libraries are repo-only and inlined, so they are not released.
